[Login] Integrate Login Email (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN auth (src/components/user-sign, src/services/environment.js) authenticates against the GoThru APIs and stores token / tokenApil / gothru_uid (see docs/analyze.md §2.8 and §3.4).

Goal

Implement email/password login in the Flutter app: the user signs in with email + password, the app authenticates against the GoThru API, and the session token + user identity are persisted for subsequent API calls.

Scope

  • Login screen with email + password fields and validation.
  • Call the GoThru auth endpoint; on success store token/tokenApil/gothru_uid (secure storage).
  • Persist session so the user stays signed in across restarts; route to Main on success.
  • Surface auth errors (wrong credentials, network) clearly.

Out of Scope

  • Google/Apple sign-in (separate task); registration; password reset.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Valid credentials authenticate and store the session token + user id.
  • Session persists across app restarts (auto-login until logout/expiry).
  • Invalid credentials show a clear error; no crash.
  • Email/password fields validated before submit; labels via i18n.
  • On success the user lands on Main.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Login with valid credentials (happy path)

  1. Enter a valid email + password → Sign In.
  2. Expected: Login succeeds; user lands on Main; session token stored.

TC-2 — Invalid credentials

  1. Enter a wrong password.
  2. Expected: Clear "invalid credentials" error; user stays on login.

TC-3 — Field validation

  1. Submit with empty/invalid email or empty password.
  2. Expected: Inline validation; submit blocked.

TC-4 — Session persistence

  1. Log in, force-close and relaunch the app.
  2. Expected: User remains signed in (no re-login required).

TC-5 — Offline / network error

  1. Go offline and attempt login.
  2. Expected: Clear network error message; no crash; retry possible.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language and view login.
  2. Expected: Labels/validation/errors translated; no raw keys.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: other auth methods unaffected once added.

[Login] Integrate Login Google (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN uses Google Sign-In (@react-native-google-signin) and stores google_token/google_access_token alongside the GoThru session (see docs/analyze.md §2.8, §3.4).

Goal

Implement Google Sign-In in the Flutter app: the user authenticates with Google, the app exchanges/validates with the GoThru API, and the session + Google tokens are persisted.

Scope

  • "Continue with Google" button -> native Google sign-in flow.
  • Obtain Google token, authenticate with GoThru, store token/tokenApil/gothru_uid + google_token/google_access_token.
  • Persist session across restarts; route to Main on success.
  • Handle cancel and failure cases.

Out of Scope

  • Email and Apple sign-in (separate tasks); Google Drive backup integration.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Google sign-in completes and creates a valid GoThru session.
  • Google + GoThru tokens stored securely; session persists across restarts.
  • User-cancelled sign-in returns to login cleanly (no error spam).
  • Failures (network / denied) surfaced clearly; on success lands on Main.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Google sign-in (happy path)

  1. Tap Continue with Google -> choose an account -> grant consent.
  2. Expected: Signs in; lands on Main; session stored.

TC-2 — User cancels

  1. Start Google sign-in and cancel the account chooser.
  2. Expected: Returns to login; no error toast/crash.

TC-3 — Session persistence

  1. Sign in with Google, relaunch the app.
  2. Expected: Still signed in.

TC-4 — Network error

  1. Go offline and attempt Google sign-in.
  2. Expected: Clear network error; retry possible.

TC-5 — Account with no GoThru access (if applicable)

  1. Use a Google account not provisioned on GoThru.
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully with an informative message.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language and view login.
  2. Expected: Button/labels/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS (requires Google services configured)
Regression watch: email login still works alongside Google.

QA Summary - Issue #17: Login Google

Verdict: BUG FOUND

Test Evidence

Item Result
Manual real-mobile validation Completed by QA tester using testpanorra@gmail.com.
Supporting automated check flutter test test/auth_service_test.dart passed: 8/8 tests.
Coding defect Offline Google Sign-In error/alert is not informative, failing TC-4.

Manual Real-Mobile Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 Gray Box Google Sign-In using the tester account. Google and GoThru authentication complete and Main opens. Completed successfully. Pass
TC-2 Black Box Cancel the native Google account chooser. Return to Login with no error toast or crash. Returned cleanly; no crash/error spam. Pass
TC-3 Gray Box Force-close and relaunch after Google Sign-In. Stored session restores directly to Main. Session persisted after relaunch. Pass
TC-4 Black Box Disable network and start Google Sign-In. An informative network error explains the problem and retry is possible. An alert appears, but its message does not clearly tell the user that the device is offline / that internet connectivity is required. Fail — coding bug
TC-5 Black Box Google account without GoThru access, if applicable. Informative access-denied handling. Not required for the provisioned tester account; source path has a handled notRegistered outcome. N/A
TC-6 White Box Review Google Login UI/localization. Google button and related text render without raw localization keys. Rendered normally. Pass
REG-1 Gray Box Email/password login after Google-flow checks. Email login remains available. No regression observed. Pass

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Native Google flow GoogleSignInService.signIn() invokes the native chooser and returns an ID token. Correct.
Cancel handling Platform code sign_in_canceled returns null; AuthController treats it as no error. Correct.
Token/session persistence AuthService.loginWithGoogle() validates the ID token, gets session/tokenApil, then stores Google and GoThru session fields securely. Correct.
Session restoration AuthController.restoreSession() restores a valid stored session at app start. Correct.
Offline error mapping GoogleSignInService categorizes non-cancel platform failures only as generic platformError; googleSignInErrorMessage() emits generic/signing-key guidance rather than a dedicated offline message. Defect confirmed.
Regression check Focused auth service suite passed 8/8. Passed, but does not cover native Google offline messaging.

API / Session Flow Review

Step Application flow Result
1 Native Google Sign-In returns an ID token. Passed in real-mobile validation.
2 POST /auth/validate validates the Google identity and reads gothru_uid. Passed in real-mobile validation.
3 GET /login/{idToken} establishes GoThru session data. Passed in real-mobile validation.
4 POST /auth/check-session?ec=false obtains tokenApil. Passed in real-mobile validation.
5 Secure store persists google_token, google_access_token, and GoThru session fields. Passed by relaunch validation.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Valid Google login reaches Main and persists Observed True Positive 2
User cancellation must not authenticate or error Observed clean return to Login True Negative 1
Offline login must show an informative network error Non-informative alert observed False Negative 1
Cancel/invalid state incorrectly grants Main access Not observed False Positive 0

Developer Bug

Google Sign-In offline alert is not informative.

When the device has no network and the user starts Google Sign-In, the application presents an alert that does not clearly state that internet connectivity is unavailable or how to recover. This fails the issue's TC-4/acceptance requirement for a clear network failure message.

Suggested correction: classify native Google platform/network failures separately from signing-key/configuration failures and show a concise user-facing message such as: No internet connection. Check your connection and try again. Keep diagnostic error codes only in debug logs.

Conclusion

WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-30.at.09.58.33.mp4

Core Google Sign-In, cancellation handling, session persistence, localization, and email-login regression passed on the real mobile app. Issue #17 remains failed because the offline error is not informative, a confirmed application-code error-handling defect.

[Profile] Integrate Profile (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN profile screen (src/pages/profile) shows the signed-in user's account info; see docs/analyze.md §2.8.

Update: Logout stays in the sidebar — matching current production (the Logout item at the bottom of the sidebar Main Menu, below "Visit GoThru"). Do not move logout onto the Profile screen; Profile is for viewing account details only.

Goal

Implement the Profile screen in Flutter: display the signed-in user's account details (name, email, avatar). Logout is not part of this screen — it remains the sidebar's Logout action, as in current production.

Scope

  • Profile screen showing user identity (name, email, avatar) from the stored session / GoThru API.
  • Loading and error states.
  • Sidebar Logout (keep as production): the Logout entry remains in the sidebar (bottom of Main Menu); tapping it clears the session/tokens and returns to Login.

Out of Scope

  • Subscription (separate task), Sync Profile (separate task), editing profile fields, account deletion.
  • Relocating logout into the Profile screen (explicitly excluded — keep it in the sidebar).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Profile shows the current user's name, email, and avatar.
  • The Profile screen does not contain a logout button.
  • The sidebar retains its Logout action (bottom of Main Menu), styled/placed as in current production.
  • Sidebar Logout clears session/tokens and routes to Login.
  • Loading and error states handled; labels via i18n.
  • After logout, protected screens are not reachable without re-login.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — View profile (happy path)

  1. Sign in → open Profile.
  2. Expected: Correct name, email, avatar displayed; no logout button on the Profile screen.

TC-2 — Logout from sidebar

  1. Open the sidebar → tap Logout (bottom of Main Menu).
  2. Expected: Session cleared; app returns to Login; cannot go back into the app without re-login.

TC-3 — Logout placement matches production

  1. Open the sidebar.
  2. Expected: Logout appears at the bottom of the Main Menu (below "Visit GoThru"), consistent with current production.

TC-4 — Avatar / missing fields

  1. View a profile with no avatar or a missing field.
  2. Expected: Placeholder shown; no crash or blank screen.

TC-5 — Persistence

  1. Open Profile, relaunch app, open Profile again.
  2. Expected: Still shows the signed-in user (until logout).

TC-6 — Offline

  1. Open Profile while offline.
  2. Expected: Cached identity shown where available; clear handling if data unavailable.

TC-7 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Profile + sidebar Logout labels translated; no raw keys.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: sidebar Logout still works; logout does not leave stale tokens that allow API calls.

[Profile] Integrate Subscription (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN reads per-user storage/plan via GET /v1/users/detail-storage on the listings API (apil.gothru.co), used for quota display (see docs/analyze.md §2.7, §3.4).

Goal

Implement the Subscription / Plan section in Profile: fetch and display the user's current plan and storage usage/quota from the GoThru API.

Scope

  • Fetch subscription/storage detail (detail-storage) for the signed-in user.
  • Display plan tier and storage used vs total (with a usage indicator).
  • Loading, empty, and error states; refresh on open.

Out of Scope

  • In-app purchase / plan upgrade flow; payment; Sync Profile.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Subscription view shows current plan and storage used/total.
  • Values reflect the GoThru API response (used vs total quota).
  • Loading and error states handled; works after token is set.
  • Labels/formatting (sizes, %) localized.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — View subscription (happy path)

  1. Sign in → Profile → Subscription.
  2. Expected: Plan + storage used/total displayed, matching the account.

TC-2 — Storage usage indicator

  1. View for an account with meaningful usage.
  2. Expected: Usage bar/percent reflects used÷total correctly.

TC-3 — Near/over quota

  1. View an account close to or over its quota (if available).
  2. Expected: Clear indication of high/exceeded usage; no overflow/format break.

TC-4 — Network / API error

  1. Go offline or simulate API failure.
  2. Expected: Clear error state with retry; no crash.

TC-5 — Refresh

  1. Open subscription, pull-to-refresh / reopen.
  2. Expected: Values re-fetched and updated.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels and size/percent formatting localized.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: profile identity display unaffected by the subscription fetch.

[Profile] Integrate Sync Profile (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN refreshes the signed-in user's account data from the GoThru API and updates the in-memory/session state (see docs/analyze.md §2.8, §3.4). In the offline-first app, profile data must be re-synced when connectivity returns.

Goal

Implement Sync Profile in Flutter: refresh the user's profile/account data from the GoThru API and update local session/cache, so the profile reflects the latest server state.

Scope

  • A sync action (manual trigger and/or on Profile open / app foreground) that fetches the latest profile from the API.
  • Update local cache/session with fresh data (name, email, avatar, plan/quota linkage).
  • Sync status feedback (in-progress / success / failure); skip gracefully when offline.

Out of Scope

  • Two-way sync / editing profile on device; subscription purchase.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Sync fetches the latest profile and updates the displayed data.
  • Sync status surfaced (loading/success/error).
  • Offline: sync is skipped/queued gracefully — no crash, clear messaging.
  • Stale local data is replaced by server data on successful sync.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Manual sync (happy path)

  1. On Profile, trigger Sync.
  2. Expected: Latest profile data fetched and displayed; success indicated.

TC-2 — Server-side change reflected

  1. Change the user's profile on the server, then Sync in-app.
  2. Expected: The updated value appears after sync.

TC-3 — Offline sync

  1. Go offline and trigger Sync.
  2. Expected: Clear "offline" handling; no crash; syncs later when online (if queued).

TC-4 — Sync failure

  1. Simulate an API error during sync.
  2. Expected: Error state shown; previous data preserved; retry possible.

TC-5 — Auto-sync on foreground (if implemented)

  1. Background the app, change data server-side, foreground it.
  2. Expected: Profile refreshes per the defined trigger.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Sync status/labels translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: sync does not clobber the session token or force a logout on transient errors.

[Tour Detail] Integrate List Panorama (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: Tour Detail lists a project's panoramas grouped by level (docs/analyze.md §2.4, §3.2 project-detail, §3.3 panoramas/levels). Panoramas are read from the local DB and shown with thumbnails, ordered by increment/order_sequence.

Goal

Implement the panorama list in Tour Detail for the Flutter app: load a project's panoramas from the local DB and render them as a scrollable, ordered list/grid with thumbnails — the foundation other Tour Detail actions (add/delete/info) operate on.

Scope

  • Query panoramas for the open project from the local DB.
  • Render thumbnails in correct order (increment / order_sequence), grouped by level where applicable.
  • Show per-item basics (thumbnail, filename/index, upload/sync indicator, hidden state).
  • Loading, empty, and error states; efficient scrolling for large lists.
  • List refreshes when panoramas are added/removed/reordered.

Out of Scope

  • Add/Delete/Info actions and reordering logic (separate tasks) — this task provides the list they plug into.
  • Upload to GoThru; map editing.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Tour Detail shows the project's panoramas from the local DB.
  • Items render thumbnails in the correct order, grouped by level where relevant.
  • Hidden (hide) and not-yet-uploaded panoramas are visually distinguishable.
  • Loading / empty / error states handled.
  • List performs smoothly with a large number of panoramas.
  • List reflects changes (add/remove) without an app restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — List renders (happy path)

  1. Open a tour that has several panoramas.
  2. Expected: All panoramas appear with thumbnails, in the correct order.

TC-2 — Empty state

  1. Open a tour with no panoramas.
  2. Expected: A clear empty state is shown (no spinner stuck, no crash).

TC-3 — Ordering

  1. Open a tour where panoramas have a defined order.
  2. Expected: Display order matches increment / order_sequence (not random).

TC-4 — Grouping by level

  1. Open a tour with panoramas across multiple levels.
  2. Expected: Panoramas are grouped/labeled under their level.

TC-5 — Status indicators

  1. View a tour mixing uploaded, local-only, and hidden panoramas.
  2. Expected: Upload/sync and hidden states are visually distinguishable and correct.

TC-6 — Large list performance

  1. Open a tour with many panoramas (e.g. 50+).
  2. Expected: Smooth scrolling; thumbnails load without freezing the UI.

TC-7 — Reflects changes

  1. Add or remove a panorama (via the respective flows) and return to the list.
  2. Expected: The list updates immediately to reflect the change.

TC-8 — Persistence / offline

  1. Open the tour offline, then relaunch the app and reopen.
  2. Expected: The same panoramas render from the local DB with no network dependency.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: opening the list does not modify any panorama data or order.
